summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and a history of Puestow procedure was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain lasting three weeks, associated with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. The pain was described as a deep epigastric ache radiating to the left side and back, different from his usual pattern, and exacerbated by a symptomatic ventral hernia. He reported syncopal episodes with incontinence during severe pain, previously evaluated as likely pseudoseizures. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction or free air. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control with IV then oral Dilaudid, and temporary dietary restriction. His insulin was adjusted due to hypoglycemia on admission, with Lantus reduced from 10 to 5 units at bedtime. He tolerated advancement to a regular diet, and his symptoms improved. He was discharged home with instructions to continue medications, follow up with his primary care provider, and attend scheduled mental health appointments.
